source_anchors.operation: getCompensationVoltages scans all spectra, collects CVs of spectra whose drift time unit is FAIMS_COMPENSATION_VOLTAGE, returns an empty set without FAIMS spectra, and ignores DRIFTTIME_NOT_SET with a warning
early return for an experiment without spectra, then an any_of pre-scan for a FAIMS spectrum (30-38); both only return the empty set that collection would also yield
CVs.insert(spec.getDriftTime()) into std::set<double> with no NaN check
CVs.erase(IMTypes::DRIFTTIME_NOT_SET) > 0 logs 'Warning: FAIMS compensation voltage is missing for at least one spectrum!' with OPENMS_LOG_WARN

an identification with a FAIMS_CV meta value (metaValueExists) is converted with (double)getMetaValue and kept when std::abs(pep_cv - target_cv) < cv_tolerance (strict); neither target_cv nor cv_tolerance is checked, so an infinite target is filtered and keeps only unannotated identifications (oracle target_positive_infinity, target_negative_infinity)
identifications without a FAIMS_CV annotation are kept in every group for backward compatibility
operator double throws ConversionError for EMPTY_VALUE, converts INT_VALUE, and otherwise reads data_.dou_ (CPP-058 for strings and lists)
setValue stores any DataValue, EMPTY included, so metaValueExists reports an empty annotation
splitByFAIMSCV groups spectra by the voltage set, in set order

evidence: Tier 1 (executed differential, oracle-generated): the unmodified product-sdk libOpenMS (Debug, core 4fdec46; git diff 4fdec46..bc9cc12 empty for FAIMSHelper.{h,cpp}, FAIMSHelper_test.cpp, IM_FAIMS_test.mzML, MzMLHandler.cpp, DataValue.cpp, MetaInfo.cpp, IMTypes.h and Constants.h; installed FAIMSHelper.h equal to the pin) executed getCompensationVoltages on IM_FAIMS_test.mzML and on 16 synthetic experiments, and filterPeptidesByFAIMSCV under 13 parameter cases on nine identifications (NaN, +inf and -inf targets at tolerance 0.01 and at an infinite tolerance among them), on an empty list, on an empty annotation, and with +inf and -inf targets against +inf, -inf and -45 annotations. The Rust voltages equal the C++ sets bit for bit, including the sign of zero, in iteration order, for every case without a FAIMS NaN. The Rust filter keeps exactly the C++ identifiers for the nine accepted cases, including the four infinite-target cases, where C++ throws nothing and keeps only the unannotated identifications. On the representable identifications of the infinite-annotation cases it also keeps what C++ keeps; C++ matches no infinite annotation, not even the same infinity. The three NaN voltage cases, the five silent parameter cases (NaN target at both tolerances, zero, negative and NaN tolerance) and the empty annotation are refused natively, and their recorded C++ outcomes are asserted. The oracle stderr carries the missing-voltage warning three times (class_section_beyond_first_and_sentinel, only_sentinel, nan_first); Rust warns for the first two and refuses the third. Tier 3: the five FAIMSHelper_test.cpp sections are transcribed unchanged. Tier 4: CompensationVoltage ordering, equality and hashing, the refusals and the ceilings. filterPeptidesByFAIMSCV has no upstream class test; the oracle is its only executed evidence. No Debug-only precondition lies on this path.
